correctness.rationale: Re-audited the narrowed theorem in repairs/5/RESULT.md. The displayed divergence follows from differentiating rP and completing the square; at the maximum allowed mu its zero set is one point, so recurrence exclusion by strictly negative area integral still holds, including a loop through the hyperbolic saddle. The positive-radius equilibrium determinants have opposite signs and the second trace is negative; the axis equilibrium is a sink. If a reversed stable branch stays below sqrt(5), bounded radial forcing allows infinite continuation, and once |z|>1 the sign of the linear height equation traps it there and the positive lower bound for P forces radial growth. Otherwise the branch would be bounded in both directions and the planar limit-set alternatives force a backward equilibrium. Neither forward sink can be a nonstationary backward limit, and the remaining saddle would give a forbidden homoclinic loop. This works separately for both branches. Past sqrt(5) radius is increasing; it reaches sqrt(10) since z cannot diverge at finite time under bounded radial forcing. For r^2>=10, (r^2-5)(21r^2-20)>=19r^4/2, giving reversed radial growth at least (19*mu/42)r^5. This bounds both the remaining time and the integral of r^2 up to the endpoint, so variation of constants yields a finite z_*. Then h=r^(-4) has derivative 4*mu+O(r^-2); integration first gives h comparable to Delta and then h=4*mu*Delta+O(Delta^(3/2)). Integrating the height equation gives the claimed negative coefficient, and the exact identity theta+ez-t=constant gives the positive signed phase coefficient (for e=0 the phase increment is exactly Delta). Both ends going to unbounded radius prove properness; the planar Jordan separation argument and rotation give the stated cylinder and common boundary. The axis is interior to the origin basin. The proof needs no finite trajectory simulation.
residual_risks: The big-O constants are not uniform as mu tends to zero; the endpoint heights and times are branch-dependent. No assertion of Cartesian Hurwitzness throughout the dynamical parameter range is made.

It rules out trapping and height escape at bounded radius on either entire branch, and identifies the anisotropic endpoint behavior: diverging radius, finite height, and finite lifted phase.
